title: 1tqhx6b
Differences in worship and belief
hook: The same Qur'an, the same Prophet: what reading does the Ja'fari practice in the call to prayer, the prayer and the prostration rest on?
scenes.0.text: The adhan is the call that Bilal recited in the Prophet's time. There are reports that Ibn Umar and Abu Mahdhura at times used the phrase "Hayya ala khayr al-amal." Their authenticity is disputed; the practice is reported as having been abandoned later. The Ja'fari school maintains this phrase as an original part of the adhan. It is also reported that Caliph Umar removed it.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 39sy1h
Bilal
scenes.1.text: In Ja'fari jurisprudence, "Hayya ala khayr al-amal" is a part of the adhan. It is reported that Caliph Umar removed it on the grounds that it weakens the fighting spirit. According to the view of today's Shia scholars, "Ashhadu anna Aliyyan waliyyullah" is not a condition of the adhan; it is recited as a recommended emblem (shi'ar). "As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm" is not recited in the Ja'fari adhan. This last phrase is mentioned in some schools of jurisprudence as an established sunna in the dawn adhan.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 1h556w8
Muezzin
scenes.2.text: In the Maliki school, letting the hands hang down in prayer is relayed as one opinion. In most of the other Sunni schools the hands are folded while standing, and this is considered sunna. In Ja'fari jurisprudence the hands are left at the sides; folding them is regarded as invalidating the prayer. Letting them hang down is maintained as the practice of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: q33sx7
Worshipper
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: q33sx7
Worshipper
scenes.3.text: In the report from Jabir it is said, "The earth has been made for me and my community a place of prostration and a means of purification (tayammum)." Ja'fari jurisprudence makes the prostration on something that grows from the ground and is neither eaten nor worn, and on earth; it regards prostration on earth as a condition. For this reason many Shia carry a prostration stone, a turba. Earth from Karbala is especially preferred. In the Sunni schools the place of prostration may be a carpet, a mat or earth.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1br6cqq
In prostration
scenes.4.text: The cherishing of the earth of Karbala is connected with its being the place where Imam Husayn was martyred. In some reports, healing and reward are attached to this earth. The chain-of-transmission value of these reports is disputed even among Shia scholars. In Shia jurisprudence, prostration on earth is sunna, and earth from Karbala is regarded as recommended. Using a prostration stone is not forbidden in the Sunni schools. The Ja'fari school regards prostration on what grows from the ground as a continuation of the Prophet's practice of prostration.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.5.text: Ibn Abbas relates that the Prophet combined the noon and afternoon, and the sunset and night prayers, in Medina without fear, rain or travel. The reason was not to burden his community. Ja'fari jurisprudence maintains this practice as combining without excuse. The times are shared from noon to sunset and from sunset to midnight; praying them separately is more virtuous. In the Sunni schools the same hadith is mostly interpreted as a special excuse. The Hanafis do not accept combining except in narrow circumstances such as travel and the day of Arafa.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.text: When Caliph Umar saw people scattered on a Ramadan night, he gathered them behind Ubayy b. Ka'b and said, "What a good innovation (bid'a) this is." In the Sunni schools, tarawih is sunna; this gathering is regarded as legitimate with the acceptance of the Companions. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, the Ramadan night supererogatory prayer is performed individually. Tarawih in congregation is not regarded as a sunna of the Prophet; this gathering is Caliph Umar's practice. His word "bid'a" is also remembered in this reading.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.7.text: Anfal 8:41 says that one fifth of what is taken as spoils belongs to God, the Prophet, relatives, orphans, the poor and travelers. Ja'fari jurisprudence reads "spoils" broadly; one fifth is given from the surplus of annual earnings. The khums is two equal parts: the Imam's share, and the share of the sayyids, that is, of the orphans, poor and travelers from among the Hashimites. In the period of occultation, the Imam's share is spent under the supervision of the mujtahid. In the Sunni schools the verse is considered valid for war spoils, and no khums is taken from earnings. The acceptance of the verse is shared; the difference lies in its scope.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: 16pen9g
Merchant
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: xbhgan
Mujtahid
scenes.8.text: Al Imran 3:28 ("except that you guard yourselves against them") and Nahl 16:106 ("except for one who is compelled while his heart is full of faith") are the verses of this dispensation. The report is known that Ammar b. Yasir, under torture, spoke a word of denial with his tongue and that the Prophet said to him, "If they do it again, say it again." In Ja'fari jurisprudence, taqiyya is permissible in danger to life, property and honor and when the school must be protected, and sometimes it is obligatory. Because Shia lived under pressure in history, this ruling found a place in jurisprudence. The same verses are cited as grounds; taqiyya is mentioned as a dispensation in hardship such as danger to life.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: sf7oxz
Ammar b. Yasir
scenes.9.text: The Ghadir hadith, "Whoever I am his mawla, Ali is also his mawla," is also found in Sunni books. Whether the word "mawla" means leadership or friendship is discussed separately. Ashura is a fast day mentioned in al-Bukhari; the deliverance of Musa is remembered, and the martyrdom of Imam Husayn is also recalled. In the Ja'fari tradition, the first ten days of Muharram and Ashura are the mourning of Karbala. 18 Dhu al-Hijja is regarded as the festival of Ghadir.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.10.text: Ahzâb 33:33 says, "God only wishes to remove impurity from you and to make you thoroughly pure, O Ahl al-Bayt." In the Kisa hadith in Muslim, the Prophet takes Imam Ali, Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under his cloak and recites this verse. In al-Bukhari 6585, the Prophet says that some of his companions will be driven away from the Pool (hawd). The Ja'fari reading regards the verse of purification as evidence for the infallibility (isma) of the Ahl al-Bayt; it measures the justice of the Companions by a person's conduct and knowledge. In the Sunni tradition, love for the Ahl al-Bayt is important, and infallibility is regarded as specific to the prophets. The hadith of the Pool is attributed to apostates or hypocrites.
scenes.10.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.10.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
sunni.0.says: Caliph Umar gathers people behind Ubayy b. Ka'b on a Ramadan night and says, "What a good innovation (bid'a) this is"; he also says that the prayer performed in the last part of the night is more virtuous.
sunni.1.says: The Prophet says that some of his companions will be driven away at the Pool; the answer is given, "You do not know what they innovated after you."
sunni.2.says: From Jabir: "The earth has been made for me and my community a place of prostration and a means of purification (tayammum)." In Sunni sources it is cited as evidence that earth is a place of prostration.
sunni.3.says: Ibn Abbas says that the Prophet combined the noon and afternoon, and the sunset and night prayers, in Medina without fear or rain, and that the reason was not to put his community in hardship.
sunni.4.says: The Prophet takes Imam Ali, Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under his cloak and recites the verse Ahzâb 33:33.
sunni.5.says: The differences in reports about the wording of the adhan; the report that Ibn Umar said "hayya ala khayr al-amal" is known from secondary sources, and its authenticity is disputed.
sunni.6.says: The relaying of the Maliki school's opinion on letting the hands hang down in prayer (sadl); the report of Caliph Umar concerning the Ramadan night prayer (qiyam).
sunni.7.says: The Ghadir hadith is also found in Sunni hadith books.
shia.0.says: Reports from the imams on the adhan, khums and taqiyya, and the meaning of Ghadir.
shia.1.says: The reports on which Shia jurisprudence rests concerning the place of "Hayya ala khayr al-amal" in the adhan, letting the hands hang down, combining prayers and the place of prostration.
shia.2.says: Reports on making prostration on what grows from the ground, prostration on the earth of Karbala, and the distribution of khums.
shia.3.says: A summary of the Shia view and the scholars' details.
disputes.0.title: 1bgyqqm
The phrases of the adhan
disputes.0.shia: The phrase "Hayya ala khayr al-amal" is mentioned in some early reports. In Ja'fari jurisprudence it is a part of the adhan; the testimony to Imam Ali is not a condition but a recommended emblem. "As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm" is not recited in the Ja'fari adhan.
disputes.0.sunni: The phrase "Hayya ala khayr al-amal" is mentioned in some early reports. In the Sunni adhan this phrase is not recited; "as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm" is the sunna of the dawn adhan. There are also reports concerning Ibn Umar.
disputes.1.title: efgmld
The position of the arms
disputes.1.shia: The position of the hand in prayer is discussed in both jurisprudences. In Ja'fari practice the hands hang down; folding them is regarded as invalidating the prayer.
disputes.1.sunni: The position of the hand in prayer is discussed in both jurisprudences. In the majority the hands are folded; in the Maliki school the opinion of letting them hang down has also been relayed.
disputes.2.title: 1s6b0ve
The prostration stone (turba)
disputes.2.shia: Prostration on earth has evidence in both traditions. In Ja'fari jurisprudence prostration is made on what grows from the ground; earth from Karbala is recommended.
disputes.2.sunni: Prostration on earth has evidence in both traditions. In the Sunni schools the place of prostration is free; al-Bukhari 335 reports that the earth was made a place of prostration.
disputes.3.title: 8x097a
Combining prayers
disputes.3.shia: The hadith that the Prophet combined prayers in Medina is mentioned in both sources. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, combining without excuse is permissible; praying separately is more virtuous.
disputes.3.sunni: The hadith that the Prophet combined prayers in Medina is mentioned in both sources. The Sunni schools mostly tie this combining to an excuse (Muslim, Sahih).
disputes.4.title: fs4ose
Tarawih
disputes.4.shia: That Caliph Umar gathered the congregation on a Ramadan night also appears in al-Bukhari 2010. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, tarawih in congregation is not sunna; the supererogatory prayer is performed individually.
disputes.4.sunni: That Caliph Umar gathered the congregation on a Ramadan night also appears in al-Bukhari 2010. In the Sunni schools tarawih is sunna and is regarded as legitimate with the acceptance of the Companions.
disputes.5.title: 67piz1
Khums
disputes.5.shia: The one-fifth ruling of Anfal 8:41 is accepted in both schools. In Ja'fari jurisprudence khums is paid on annual earnings; there are the Imam's share and the sayyids' share.
disputes.5.sunni: The one-fifth ruling of Anfal 8:41 is accepted in both schools. In the Sunni schools the verse is specific to war spoils; no khums is taken from earnings.
disputes.6.title: 1x2xti7
Taqiyya
disputes.6.shia: The dispensation to speak under duress is mentioned in both sources, with the Ammar incident and the related verses. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, taqiyya is permissible in danger to life, property and honor, and sometimes obligatory.
disputes.6.sunni: The dispensation to speak under duress is mentioned in both sources, with the Ammar incident and the related verses. In Sunni jurisprudence, taqiyya is a dispensation at the moment of coercion; it is not regarded as a constant principle.
disputes.7.title: lcke7z
Ashura and Ghadir
disputes.7.shia: The day of Ashura and the Ghadir hadith are known in both traditions. In the Ja'fari calendar, Ashura is mourning and 18 Dhu al-Hijja is the festival of Ghadir.
disputes.7.sunni: The day of Ashura and the Ghadir hadith are known in both traditions. In Sunni practice Ashura is a fast day; the word "mawla" is interpreted as friendship.
disputes.8.title: 1jkwlfn
Infallibility and the justice of the Companions
disputes.8.shia: The verse of purification and the Kisa hadith mention the Ahl al-Bayt in both sources. In Ja'fari belief the Ahl al-Bayt are infallible (ma'sum) through this verse; the justice of the Companions depends on a measure.
disputes.8.sunni: The verse of purification and the Kisa hadith mention the Ahl al-Bayt in both sources. In Sunni belief all the Companions are just; infallibility is specific to the prophets. The hadith of the Pool is attributed to apostates or hypocrites.
questions.0: If in Muslim the Prophet's combining is explained as "not to put his community in hardship," how does this reason help in understanding the prayer times?
questions.1: If the hadith that the earth was made a place of prostration is in both sources, does the difference in the place of prostration stand between the condition of earth and freedom?
questions.2: How does Caliph Umar's calling tarawih a "good innovation" bring his own word to the fore in whether an act of worship is regarded as sunna or not?
questions.3: How does Ammar b. Yasir's word under duress show the limit of taqiyya with respect to life and faith?
questions.4: How do the hadith of the Pool (al-Bukhari 6585), love for the Companions and the measuring of conduct stand side by side?
summary: Differences such as the adhan, the position of the hands, the place of prostration, combining, tarawih, khums and taqiyya arise from two readings of the same verses and hadiths. The Ja'fari school explains them as a continuation of the Qur'an and the Prophet's practice. The Sunni schools too draw their own practices from the same texts.
key: Differences in the adhan, prayer and prostration
notes.0: In the adhan, «Hayya ala khayr al-amal» is recited in Shia jurisprudence, «as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm» is not.
notes.1: In prayer the hands are left hanging in Shia jurisprudence, and folded in most Sunni schools.
notes.2: In Shia jurisprudence prostration is made on earth or on something that grows from the ground; in the Sunni schools it is free.
notes.3: The practices of combining prayers, tarawih and khums are different.
notes.4: Ashura is for commemorating the suffering of Karbala; Ghadir, however, is the joy of Imam Ali's wilayat.
